Q: If greater than batch files A:

Try this:

if 3 gtr 2 @echo "biggger"

This outputs:

"biggger"

The other operators are:

  • EQU - equal
  • NEQ - not equal
  • LSS - less than
  • LEQ - less than or equal
  • GTR - greater than
  • GEQ - greater than or equal

Q: Threading flask and while loop A:

Python argument list is always evaluated first and the result is then passed to the function being called. In your case app.run() is executed/evaluated first, and then it's passed to threading.Thread() as its argument. That's why you notice it's executed first because Python needs to get the result from app.run() first. So if that argument is changed to app.run then it is a method object instead of calling for its result. You can then pass such object to threading.Thread()'s keyword parameter target= so in that function in can executed in its separate thread.

The same goes to loop(), which should be changed to loop so the code can pass another method object to threading.Thread() to execute in another separate thread. Without doing so, you are simply executing the loop in the main thread.

So these 2 lines:

thread1 = threading.Thread(target=app.run())
thread2 = threading.Thread(target=loop())

should be changed to:

thread1 = threading.Thread(target=app.run)
thread2 = threading.Thread(target=loop)

Q: Configuring WCF client gives the error "The message could not be processed. This is most likely because the action A:

You most likely have a service contract mismatch on the ITestingWebService interface. Try running a "Update Service Reference" by right clicking on the service reference in Visual Studio and see if that fixes the issue.

Q: How to measure the width and angle of two intersecting ropes using OpenCV? A:

Here is another way to do that in Python OpenCV.

  • Read the input image

  • Crop the right side to ensure the ropes go to it

  • Convert to gray

  • Threshold

  • Apply morphology to clean it up

  • Get Canny edges

  • Apply morphology to ensure the edges are closed

  • To first get the rope angles do the following:

  • Get the contours of the edges

  • In a loop over contours, filter on area and compute the rotated rectangle and the angle and draw the rotated rectangles on a black background

  • Sort the angles and remove the smallest and largest

  • Get the mean angle and its +90 angle as the angles of the corner of the rotated rectangle measured from vertical

  • Next to get the rope thicknesses and the angles again do the following:

  • Compute the Hough lines from the Canny edges

  • Then loop over the lines, compute the angles, the perpendicular distance from the origin and group the lines into positive and negative angles and distances and draw the lines on a copy of the input

  • Get the mean positive and negative angles

  • Print the angles

  • Sort the distances to the lines from the origin, corresponding to each of the positive and negative angles, and get the differences between successive distances as the thicknesses

  • Filter the differences for both for min and max values

  • Get the mean differences as thicknesses for both

  • Print the thicknesses

  • Save the images

Input image:

import cv2
import numpy as np
import statistics
from skimage.morphology import skeletonize
import math


# read the input image
img = cv2.imread('ropes.png')
ht, wd = img.shape[:2]

# crop the input
crop = img[0:ht, 0:wd-17]

# convert to grayscale
gray = cv2.cvtColor(crop, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)

# threshold
thresh = cv2.threshold(gray, 0, 255, cv2.THRESH_BINARY+cv2.THRESH_OTSU)[1]

# apply morphology
kernel = cv2.getStructuringElement(cv2.MORPH_ELLIPSE, (7,7))
morph = cv2.morphologyEx(thresh, cv2.MORPH_CLOSE, kernel)

# get canny edges
canny_edges = cv2.Canny(morph, threshold1=100, threshold2=200)

# apply morphology to ensure edges are closed
kernel = cv2.getStructuringElement(cv2.MORPH_ELLIPSE, (3,3))
canny_edges = cv2.morphologyEx(canny_edges, cv2.MORPH_CLOSE, kernel)


# --- GET ROPE ANGLES ---

# get contours
contours = cv2.findContours(canny_edges, cv2.RETR_EXTERNAL, cv2.CHAIN_APPROX_SIMPLE)
contours = contours[0] if len(contours) == 2 else contours[1]
#print(len(contours))

# draw red edges on morph3
edge_contours = cv2.cvtColor(morph, cv2.COLOR_GRAY2BGR)
cv2.drawContours(edge_contours, contours, -1, (0, 0, 255), thickness=2)

# get rotated rectangles for contours with large enough area
# then sort the list of angles and discard lowest and highest and get the mean
minArea = 3200
maxArea = 4200
filtered_contours = np.zeros_like(morph)
rotated_rectangles = np.zeros_like(morph)
angles = []
for cnt in contours:
    area = cv2.contourArea(cnt)
    if minArea < area < maxArea:
        # draw white filled contours on black background
        cv2.drawContours(filtered_contours, [cnt], 0, 255, -1)
        
        # get rotated rectangle
        # note: angle is measured ccw. 0, 90, 180, 270 are up-right rectangles
        rotrect = cv2.minAreaRect(cnt)
        (center), (width,height), angle = rotrect
        
        # negate angles to convert from ccw to cw from vertical
        angle = - angle
        
        # from https://www.pyimagesearch.com/2017/02/20/text-skew-correction-opencv-python/
        # the cv2.minAreaRect function returns values in the range [-90, 0)
        # for negative values larger than this range angle needs to add 90 degrees
        if angle < -45:
            angle = -(90 + angle)

        # otherwise, just take the negative of the angle to make
        # it positive
        else:
            angle = -angle

        angles.append(angle)

        # draw rotated rectangle as white outline on black background
        box = cv2.boxPoints(rotrect)
        boxpts = np.int32(box)

        cv2.drawContours(rotated_rectangles, [boxpts], 0, 255, 2)

# sort the angles list
sorted_angles = sorted(angles)

# remove smallest and largest angle from the list
filtered_angles = sorted_angles[1:-1]

# get mean of filtered angles
mean_angle = statistics.mean(filtered_angles)

# negate the angle so it is measured cw and get the two angles of the corners
mean_angle1 = mean_angle
mean_angle2 = mean_angle1 + 90
print(f"\ncorner negative angle (from vertical): {mean_angle1}")
print(f"corner positive angle (from vertical): {mean_angle2}")


# --- GET ROPE THICKNESSES ---

lines_img = img.copy()
#lines_img = cv2.cvtColor(lines_img, cv2.COLOR_GRAY2BGR)
lineThresh = 15
minLineLength = 100
maxLineGap = 35

angles_neg = []
angles_pos = []
dist_lines_neg = []
dist_lines_pos = []

lines = cv2.HoughLinesP(canny_edges, 1, np.pi/180, lineThresh, None, minLineLength, maxLineGap)

if lines is not None:
    for [line] in lines:
        x1 = line[0]
        y1 = line[1]
        x2 = line[2]
        y2 = line[3]
        
        # compute line angle from vertical and negate to change from ccw to cw
        angle_rad = math.atan2(y2 - y1, x2 - x1)
        angle_deg = math.degrees(angle_rad)
        
        # Compute perpendicular distances from origin to lines
        # see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Distance_from_a_point_to_a_line
        A = y2 - y1
        B = -(x2 - x1)
        C = (x2 * y1) - (y2 * x1)
        denominator = math.sqrt(A**2 + B**2)
        dist = abs(C) / denominator if denominator != 0 else 0
        
        # separate into negative and positive lists
        # swap dist lists as dist measured perpendicular to lines
        # and we want to associate the dist to the line angles
        if angle_deg < 0:
            angles_neg.append(angle_deg)
            dist_lines_pos.append(dist)
        else:
            angles_pos.append(angle_deg)
            dist_lines_neg.append(dist)
        
        cv2.line(lines_img, (x1, y1), (x2, y2), (0, 0, 255), 2)
else:
    print("No Lines Found")

# get mean of angles and negate to convert from ccw to cw
mean_pos_angles = statistics.mean(angles_pos) if angles_pos else 0.0
mean_neg_angles = statistics.mean(angles_neg) if angles_neg else 0.0

print(f"\nrope negative angle (from vertical): {mean_neg_angles}")
print(f"rope positive angle (from vertical): {mean_pos_angles}")

# sort perpendicular distance from origin to positive and negative angled lines 
# then compute differences between successive sorted distances
dist_lines_neg.sort()
dist_lines_pos.sort()

distances_neg = np.diff(dist_lines_neg) if len(dist_lines_neg) > 1 else np.array([])
distances_pos = np.diff(dist_lines_pos) if len(dist_lines_pos) > 1 else np.array([])

# discard distances less than 13 and greater than 30
# convert np.float64(value) to value in list
minDist = 12.0
maxDist = 30.0
filtered_distances_neg = [d for d in distances_neg if minDist <= d <= maxDist]
filtered_distances_neg = [float(x) for x in filtered_distances_neg]

filtered_distances_pos = [d for d in distances_pos if minDist <= d <= maxDist]
filtered_distances_pos = [float(x) for x in filtered_distances_pos]

# calculate the means
if filtered_distances_neg:
    mean_distance_neg = sum(filtered_distances_neg) / len(filtered_distances_neg)
else: # len is zero
    mean_distance_neg = 0

if filtered_distances_pos:
    mean_distance_pos = sum(filtered_distances_pos) / len(filtered_distances_pos)
else: # len is zero
    mean_distance_pos = 0

print("\nrope negative angle thickness:", mean_distance_neg)
print("rope positive angle thickness:", mean_distance_pos)
print("")

# save images
cv2.imwrite('ropes_thresh.png', thresh)
cv2.imwrite('ropes_morph.png', morph)
cv2.imwrite('ropes_canny_edges.png', canny_edges)
cv2.imwrite('ropes_rotated_rectangles.png', rotated_rectangles)
cv2.imwrite('ropes_hough_lines.png', lines_img)


# show images
cv2.imshow('thresh', thresh)
cv2.imshow('morph', morph)
cv2.imshow('canny edges', canny_edges)
cv2.imshow('rotated rectangles', rotated_rectangles)
cv2.imshow('hough lines', lines_img)
cv2.waitKey(0)

Q: Calculating calendar weeks from fiscal weeks A:

Assuming you have a data frame with fiscal dates of the form 'YYYYWW' where YYY = the calendar year of the start of the fiscal year and ww = the number of weeks into the year, you can convert to calendar dates as follows:

def getCalendarDate(fy_date: str):
    f_year = fy_date[0:4]
    f_week = fy_date[4:]
    fys = pd.to_datetime(f'{f_year}/10/01', format= '%Y/%m/%d')
    return fys + pd.to_timedelta(int(f_week), "W")

You can then use this function to create the column of calendar dates as follows:

df['Calendar Date]'] =  list(getCalendarDate(x) for x in df['Fiscal Week'].to_list())
